sentences.en: Have you ever noticed, when you offer a friend or a colleague or a partner a suggestion for improvement,
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现，当你向朋友、同事或伴侣提出改进建议时，

sentences.en: they often experience an urge to defend themselves?
sentences.zh: 他们往往会产生一种为自己辩护的冲动？

sentences.en: Rather than listen to how they might change or do something better, they try to preserve the status quo.
sentences.zh: 比起听取如何改变或做得更好的建议，他们更倾向于维护现状。

sentences.en: Like generals fighting a war, they try to protect every square inch of the person they are
sentences.zh: 就像打仗的将军一样，他们试图保护自己身上的每一寸领地，

sentences.en: instead of embracing the person they might become.
sentences.zh: 而不是去拥抱那个可能成为的自己。

sentences.en: In our episode last week, Winning the Battle Against Yourself,
sentences.zh: 在我们上周的节目《战胜自我》中，

sentences.en: we looked at how we often fail to make changes in our lives
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了为什么我们常常无法在生活中做出改变，

sentences.en: because our best intentions are at odds with what scientists call the value system in the brain.
sentences.zh: 因为我们最好的意图与科学家所说的脑内价值系统相悖。

sentences.en: This brain network tends to prioritize the here and now
sentences.zh: 这个大脑网络倾向于优先考虑此时此地，

sentences.en: and nudges us toward immediate gratifications instead of long-term benefits.
sentences.zh: 并促使我们追求即时满足，而不是长远利益。

sentences.en: If you missed that episode, I'd urge you to go back and listen to it in this podcast feed.
sentences.zh: 如果你错过了那期节目，我强烈建议你回过头来，在这个播客动态里听一听。

sentences.en: Today, we look at one of the most powerful reasons we fail to make changes in our lives.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来探讨我们无法在生活中做出改变的最强大原因之一。

sentences.en: Very often, the people around us can see what we need to do differently or better.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们身边的人能看出我们需要做出什么不同或更好的地方。

sentences.en: But when they tell us, when they offer us feedback, or, heaven forbid, criticism,
sentences.zh: 但当他们告诉我们、给我们反馈，或者——天哪——提出批评时，

sentences.en: we respond with anger, with denial, with defensiveness.
sentences.zh: 我们的反应却是愤怒、否认和防备。

sentences.en: This is a paradox because many of us also believe we want to live lives of continuous improvement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个悖论，因为我们许多人也相信自己想要过一种不断改进的生活。

sentences.en: What better way to improve than to listen to suggestions for improvement?
sentences.zh: 还有什么比听取改进建议更好的改进方式呢？

sentences.en: What causes so many of us to feel defensive?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致我们这么多人感到防备心重呢？

sentences.en: How can we listen better to feedback and offer feedback in a manner that will be heard?
sentences.zh: 我们怎样才能更好地倾听反馈，并以对方能够听进去的方式给出反馈呢？

sentences.en: Overcoming defensiveness as a way to improving our lives.
sentences.zh: 克服防备心理，以此改善我们的生活。
我们都经历过这种情况。

sentences.en: Someone pipes up at a work meeting to ask why we were late.
sentences.zh: 在工作会议上，有人突然插话问我们为什么迟到了。

sentences.en: Or a partner tells us we need to do a better job cleaning up after ourselves.
sentences.zh: 或者伴侣告诉我们需要把自己的善后工作做得更好。

sentences.en: A friend asks why we haven't called in a while.
sentences.zh: 朋友问我们为什么好久没打电话了。
几乎不费吹灰之力，各种借口就脱口而出。

sentences.en: If the sink was not full of dirty dishes, we would happily wash up our mugs.
sentences.zh: 如果水槽里没有堆满脏盘子，我们很乐意自己洗茶杯。

sentences.en: Did our friend not know that we have been going through a really difficult time at work?
sentences.zh: 难道我们的朋友不知道我们最近在工作上经历了一段非常艰难的时期吗？

sentences.en: At the University of Pennsylvania, psychologist Emily Falk studies the science of defensiveness
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚大学，心理学家埃米莉·福尔克研究防备心理的科学，

sentences.en: and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 以及我们能对此做些什么。

sentences.en: Emily Falk, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 埃米莉·福尔克，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
Emily, you are very close to your grandmother, Bev.
sentences.zh: 埃米莉，你和你的祖母贝芙非常亲近。

sentences.en: Recently, she shared with you her thoughts about the time that you spend with her.
sentences.zh: 最近，她和你分享了她对你花时间陪伴她的看法。

sentences.en: Can you paint a picture of what happened that evening, Emily?
sentences.zh: 埃米莉，你能描述一下那天晚上发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a typical night in my house.
sentences.zh: 对，那是我家里很典型的一个晚上。

sentences.en: And what that looks like is one of my kids was jumping up and down on the couch.
sentences.zh: 具体情况是这样的：我的一个孩子在沙发上跳上跳下。

sentences.en: The other kid was trying to show my grandmother something that he had built,
sentences.zh: 另一个孩子试图向我奶奶展示他搭的东西，

sentences.en: probably a Lego creation, like kind of really, really close up in her face.
sentences.zh: 可能是一个乐高作品，几乎快贴到她脸上了。

sentences.en: I was trying to get dinner on the table, so you can imagine sort of dishes clanging
sentences.zh: 我正试图把晚饭端上桌，所以你可以想象各种盘子的铿锵声，

sentences.en: and my phone is probably pinging with emails and text messages from people that I work with
sentences.zh: 我的手机可能也在不停地震动，收到来自同事的邮件和短信，

sentences.en: who would really like a response very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们非常希望能快点得到回复。

sentences.en: And when I was in that situation, I sort of had this sense of like,
sentences.zh: 当时身处那种情况下的我，脑子里突然有一种感觉：

sentences.en: oh my gosh, there's so many different things that I'm trying to juggle right now.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我现在要同时应付的事情太多了。

sentences.en: And in that particular moment, I decided that I was going to prioritize a little bit of time with my grandmother.
sentences.zh: 就在那个特定的时刻，我决定优先花一点时间陪陪我奶奶。

sentences.en: And my grandmother, Bev, is now 100 years old, and she's one of my very favorite people.
sentences.zh: 我奶奶贝芙现在100岁了，她是我最喜欢的人之一。

sentences.en: So she's over at my house for dinner, and I went over to her.
sentences.zh: 所以她来我家吃晚饭，我朝她走了过去。

sentences.en: I left, you know, the pasta going and handed that over to my partner to handle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我把煮着的意大利面留给了伴侣去处理。

sentences.en: And I took her hand, and I walked her outside.
sentences.zh: 我拉着她的手，带她走到了外面。

sentences.en: And sort of in the dusk, I was feeling like a little bit of a sense of relief.
sentences.zh: 在微弱的暮色中，我感觉如释重负。

sentences.en: Like I was feeling like, okay, we're getting outside.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得，好吧，我们出来了。

sentences.en: We're getting a little quality time together.
sentences.zh: 我们有一点高质量的相处时间了。

sentences.en: And I felt like I had made, you know, the right decision until she turned to me,
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己做出了正确的决定，直到她转过身来对我说，

sentences.en: and she said that even though she really liked coming to my house and seeing my kids,
sentences.zh: 尽管她真的很喜欢来我家看我的孩子们——

sentences.en: who are, you know, some of her very favorite people,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这也是她最喜欢的人中的一部分——

sentences.en: she said, we aren't really spending time together.
sentences.zh: 但她说，我们其实并没有真正在一起相处。

sentences.en: You know, it really struck me when she said that,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当她这么说的时候，真的深深触动了我，

sentences.en: because, like, I really didn't want her to be right about that.
sentences.zh: 因为，我真的不希望她是正确的。

sentences.en: Like, of course we're spending time together.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们当然是在一起相处啊。

sentences.en: Like, you're over here, I'm making dinner for all of us, and, you know, we're outside together now.
sentences.zh: 就像，你在这儿，我在为我们所有人做晚饭，而且，你知道的，我们现在不就在外面吗。

sentences.en: So what do you mean we're not spending time together?
sentences.zh: 所以你怎么能说我们没有在一起相处呢？

sentences.en: Can you just describe what went through your heart as you heard that, Emily?
sentences.zh: 埃米莉，听到这话的时候，你能描述一下你内心的感受吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you're juggling a lot.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你要应付的事情堆积如山。

sentences.en: You're kind enough to have your grandmother over at your place.
sentences.zh: 你出于好心把奶奶接到你家里来。

sentences.en: You're trying to host everyone together.
You've taken time out from this incredibly busy and stressful evening
sentences.zh: 你从这个极其忙碌和压力的夜晚抽空出来，

sentences.en: to go for a walk outside with your grandmother,
and she says you're not doing enough?
sentences.zh: 而她却说你做得还不够？

sentences.en: I definitely initially was like, no, you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我一开始绝对是觉得：不对，你错了。

sentences.en: Like, we do spend time together.
sentences.zh: 我们明明就在一起相处啊。

sentences.en: Look, what are we doing right now?
sentences.zh: 你看，我们现在在干什么？

sentences.en: It's the same kind of defensiveness that I feel when, you know,
sentences.zh: 这跟我感受到的防备心理是同一种，你知道的，

sentences.en: somebody calls me up and says, like, why haven't you called me?
sentences.zh: 当有人打电话给我并质问我“你为什么不给我打电话”时，

sentences.en: And it's like, well, we're talking right now.
sentences.zh: 我的反应就像是，好吧，我们现在不是在说话吗。

sentences.en: What do you want from me?
sentences.zh: 你还想从我这得到什么？

sentences.en: So, I mean, yeah, I definitely felt some defensiveness in that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，是的，那一刻我确实感到了一些防备心理。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how common this is?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这种情况有多普遍吗？

sentences.en: That this is a reaction that we have that I think is such a universal reaction
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们都会有的反应，我认为这是一种非常普遍的反应，

sentences.en: when someone basically gives us feedback about something that we don't want to hear.
sentences.zh: 当有人基本上对我们不想听到的事情给出反馈时。

sentences.en: And this could be somebody in our personal lives.
sentences.zh: 这可以是我们在个人生活中的某个人。

sentences.en: It could be someone in our professional lives.
sentences.zh: 它可以是我们在职业生活中的某个人。

sentences.en: It could be just a casual acquaintance.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可以只是一个泛泛之交。

sentences.en: But our first reaction very often when someone gives us feedback like this
sentences.zh: 但当有人给我们这样的反馈时，我们的第一反应往往是

sentences.en: is to dig in our heels and say, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 固执己见并说：你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think this is an incredibly common experience where, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一种极其普遍的经历，你知道的，

sentences.en: we point out something that somebody could be doing better.
sentences.zh: 我们指出某人可以做得更好的地方。

sentences.en: Like, for example, you know, maybe your partner could be taking out the trash
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，也许你的伴侣可以去倒垃圾，

sentences.en: or your kid could be doing their homework
sentences.zh: 或者你的孩子可以去做作业，

sentences.en: or somebody on your team at work could be responding to your collaborator
sentences.zh: 或者你工作团队中的某个人可以更快地回复你的合作伙伴。

sentences.en: And when we point out these things that we wish other people were doing differently,
sentences.zh: 而当我们指出这些我们希望别人做出改变的事情时，

sentences.en: the things that are most salient for them are all the things that they're already juggling.
sentences.zh: 对他们而言最显眼的事情，却是他们已经在应付的所有事情。

sentences.en: Just like you said, you know, with my grandmother,
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才说的，你知道的，关于我奶奶，

sentences.en: I was juggling a lot of different things having to do with my work and my kids
sentences.zh: 我要应付很多与工作、孩子以及准备晚饭相关的不同事情。

sentences.en: and getting dinner on the table.
And those things were front of mind for me.
sentences.zh: 这些事情当时都在我脑海的最前端。

sentences.en: And so when we point out the ways that other people could be improving their health behaviors,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们指出别人可以如何改善他们的健康行为时，

sentences.en: you know, choosing healthier activities, quitting smoking, drinking less,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，选择更健康的活动、戒烟、少喝酒、

sentences.en: getting more exercise or studying harder or, you know,
sentences.zh: 进行更多的锻炼或更努力地学习，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: making choices that are different than the choices that they're making,
sentences.zh: 做出与他们正在做的选择不同的选择，
这真的会让人感到具有威胁性。
这会威胁到我们的自我形象。

sentences.en: It can threaten our sense that we're making good choices.
sentences.zh: 这会威胁到我们“自己正在做正确选择”的信念。

sentences.en: So you say that defensiveness arises in part because the brain tends to conflate
sentences.zh: 所以你说防备心的产生部分是因为大脑倾向于将

sentences.en: what is me with what is good.
sentences.zh: “我是谁”和“什么是好的”混为一谈。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
I mean that our brain has these systems that help us think about what's good and bad,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们的大脑拥有这些系统来帮助我们思考什么是好与坏——我们的价值系统，以及帮助我们思考什么是“我”与“非我”的大脑系统，

sentences.en: our value system, and brain systems that help us think about what's me and not me,
which I call our self-relevance system.
sentences.zh: 我称之为我们的自我相关系统。

sentences.en: And the self-relevance and value systems are really intertwined with one another.
sentences.zh: 自我相关系统和价值系统是真正交织在一起的。

sentences.en: So when we make decisions about what's good and bad, it's tapping into the value system,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们对好与坏做出决定时，它是在调动价值系统，

sentences.en: but that's overlapping with our self-relevance system.
sentences.zh: 但这与我们的自我相关系统重叠了。

sentences.en: And so those kinds of decisions are conflated with one another to the degree that we tend to have these biases
sentences.zh: 因此，这类决定彼此混淆，以至于我们往往会有这样一种偏差：

sentences.en: where we think of things that are me typically on average as being good and things that are not me as being on average bad.
sentences.zh: 我们通常平均地认为属于“我”的事物是好的，而平均地认为“非我”的事物是坏的。

sentences.en: We also have optimism biases where we think of ourselves as being above average,
sentences.zh: 我们也有乐观偏差，认为自己高于平均水平，

sentences.en: like more than 50% of people think that they're an above average driver.
sentences.zh: 就像超过50%的人认为自己是高于平均水平的司机一样。

sentences.en: And so when you say, well, you know, you might not be an above average driver,
sentences.zh: 所以当你指出：嗯，你知道的，你可能不是一个高于平均水平的司机，

sentences.en: you're actually like pretty risky driver, pretty dangerous driver.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是一个相当危险的司机，一个相当具有危险性的司机。

sentences.en: People don't say, oh, thank you.
Like, I'm so glad that you pointed that out.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你指出了这一点。

sentences.en: Now I'll go and like get some lessons so that I can, you know,
sentences.zh: 现在我去上几节课，这样我就可以，你知道的，

sentences.en: be less of a danger to myself and other people on the road.
sentences.zh: 减少自己对马路上其他人和自己的危险。

sentences.en: There's the old comedy bit about how people who are driving faster than you are are maniacs
sentences.zh: 有个关于驾驶的老笑话：比你开得快的人都是疯子，

sentences.en: and people who are driving slower than you are, are, you know, super stodgy.
sentences.zh: 而比你开得慢的人，你知道的，都极其古板守旧。

sentences.en: And of course, you're driving at exactly the right speed.
sentences.zh: 当然，你自己的车速是绝对刚刚好的。

sentences.en: So I think what I'm hearing you say, Emily, is that when we're being defensive, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我想我听到你这么说，埃米莉，那就是当我们处于防备状态时，你知道的，

sentences.en: it's not just that we are trying to defend ourselves against the accusation that we might not be a good driver
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是我们试图为自己辩解，以摆脱“我们可能不是一个好司机、好伴侣或好学生”的指责。

sentences.en: or a good partner or a good student.
In some ways, we feel the attack is on us.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们觉得攻击是冲着我们来的。

sentences.en: Our sense of self is under threat.
sentences.zh: 我们的自我意识受到了威胁。

sentences.en: So I think that one of the things that can happen is that when, like, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以我想可能发生的事情之一是，当，比如，

sentences.en: when my grandma told me that she wished that we could spend more time together
sentences.zh: 当我奶奶告诉我她希望我们能花更多时间在一起时，

sentences.en: and I barely got it together to let her finish her sentence before explaining why she was wrong,
sentences.zh: 我甚至还没等她说完一整句话，就急着解释为什么她是错的，

sentences.en: that it's not just that, you know, I'm thinking about that specific situation of, like,
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为，你知道的，我在考虑那种特定情况——

sentences.en: are we actually spending quality time together right now or not?
sentences.zh: 我们现在到底是不是在进行高质量的相处？

sentences.en: But also, like, like I said to you earlier, like, am I being a good granddaughter,
sentences.zh: 而且还包括，就像我刚才对你说的，我是一个好孙女吗？

sentences.en: which is an identity that's important to me?
sentences.zh: 这是一个对我很重要的身份认同。

sentences.en: Like, am I being somebody who shows up for her family in a way that feels good for them?
sentences.zh: 我是一个能以让他们感觉舒适的方式支持家人的人吗？

sentences.en: And so this idea that, like, we cling to the idea that we're doing things right is extremely common.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种“我们坚信自己把事情做对了”的想法极其普遍。

sentences.en: Like, there's a New Yorker cartoon, I think, where there's a bunch of guys sitting around a boardroom table
sentences.zh: 就像《纽约客》上的一幅漫画，我想，里面有一群人围坐在会议桌旁

sentences.en: and the caption is, my last comment appeared to be inviting feedback, do not be fooled, right?
sentences.zh: 字幕是这样的：我刚才的评论似乎是在征求反馈，别上当，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's funny because, like, the guy is, you know, maybe he said something like he's interested in feedback,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为这个人，你知道，也许他说过类似他对比反馈感兴趣的话，

sentences.en: but everybody sitting around the table knows that what he actually wants to hear is that he's doing a great job.
sentences.zh: 但桌旁坐的每个人都知道，他真正想听的是他干得非常棒。

sentences.en: So if a sense of self that we want to protect is at the heart of defensiveness,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们想要保护的自我意识是防御心理的核心，

sentences.en: one idea to reduce this defensiveness is to make the self less salient or less prominent.
sentences.zh: 减少这种防御心理的一个思路就是让自我变得不那么显著或不那么突出。

sentences.en: You conducted a study that looked at how the practice of self-distancing affected college students' defensiveness
sentences.zh: 你做过一项研究，探讨了自我疏离的练习如何影响大学生面对

sentences.en: when it came to hearing messages about alcohol.
sentences.zh: 听到关于酒精的信息时的防御心理。

sentences.en: Tell me about that study, Emily.
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲那项研究吗，艾米丽？

sentences.en: In that study, what we had people do was we had college students who told us on a day-to-day basis
sentences.zh: 在那项研究中，我们让大学生日常向我们汇报

sentences.en: about how much they were drinking alcohol, and we randomized people into different conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们饮酒的量，并且我们把人们随机分到了不同的组别中。

sentences.en: Some of them just reacted naturally to alcohol the whole time.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人在整个过程中只是对酒精做出自然的反应。

sentences.en: Some of them were given a technique where they took the perspective of another person
sentences.zh: 另一些人则被传授了一种技术，即采纳他们社交圈中
